meetings.title: Pricing review
meetings.privateNotes: Ines wants to stop discounting annual plans. Asha worried about Q4 pipeline.
meetings.summary: We are cutting the annual discount from 20% to 10% starting next month. Data from the last two quarters: annual buyers on 20% discount churned at 9%, monthly buyers at 11%, so the discount bought us almost nothing. Asha will tell the three open deals before the change. Decision owner: Ines.
meetings.transcript: Ines: The 20% discount costs us about 40k a year and the churn gap is two points. Tomas: Two points is noise at our size. Asha: Contoso will push back, they always ask for 25. Ines: Then we lose Contoso's discount, not Contoso. We go to 10% and we say why.

meetings.title: Postmortem: report agent ran up a bill
meetings.privateNotes: Ravi embarrassed. Not a blame thing.
meetings.summary: Our nightly report agent looped on a failing chart call for 6 hours and spent $212 in model calls. Root cause: no per-run spend cap and a retry loop with no limit. Fixes: per-run cap of $2, max 40 tool calls, and an approval step before it emails customers. Since the cap went in, the worst run cost $1.84.
meetings.transcript: Tomas: The fix is boring. Cap every run, count tool calls, and make a person approve anything a customer sees. Ravi: I assumed the provider would stop it. Tomas: Nobody stops it but us.

meetings.title: Customer call: Northwind Bakery Supply
attendees: Dana Whitfield (Ops lead, Northwind Bakery Supply)
meetings.privateNotes: Dana said they might expand to 3 more sites if forecasts hold. Do not share that publicly.
meetings.summary: The customer's ops lead said the weekly demand forecast cut flour waste by 18% over 8 weeks. What they valued most was the plain-English explanation next to each forecast, not the accuracy number. They ignore the dashboard and read the Monday email.
meetings.transcript: Dana: Honestly I never open the dashboard. The Monday email tells me what changed and why, and that's what I forward to the bakers. Asha: So the explanation matters more than the chart? Dana: The explanation is the product.

meetings.title: Hiring sync
meetings.privateNotes: Candidate A asked for 30% above band.
meetings.summary: We dropped the take-home test. Over the last 14 candidates, 6 dropped out at the take-home stage, and the 3 people we hired did no better on it than the ones we passed on. Replacing it with a 45-minute paired debugging session on a real bug from our tracker.
meetings.transcript: Tomas: The take-home measured free time, not skill. Ines: Then we stop asking for free time.

meetings.title: Q1 roadmap
meetings.privateNotes: Board wants an AI story. Ines skeptical.
meetings.summary: Q1 priority is the explanation layer, not a chatbot. Three customers asked for a chat interface; eleven asked for better explanations in the Monday email. We build for the eleven.
meetings.transcript: Ines: A chatbot demos well. Explanations renew. We build what renews.
